answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with mutual credit lines: each agent grants limited credit to counterparties it trusts, and value moves only along these trust edges. A newborn identity starts with zero incoming credit, so ten thousand Sybils cannot pool more liquidity than one node grants them — the attack cost grows with every relationship forged, like a zephyr against a fortress wall. Genuine agents expand their credit horizon gradually as good history accrues, while attackers face a spiral of declining trust the moment any Sybil defaults.
